# 1 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_012_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Jonathan saw that the time was right for him, and he chose men and sent them to Rome to confirm and renew the friendship that had previously existed between them.

**2** He also sent letters to the Spartans and to other places for the same purpose.

**3** They went to Rome, entered the senate chamber, and said: "Jonathan the high priest and the Jewish nation have sent us to renew the friendship and alliance with you, as it was in former times."

**4** The Romans gave them letters to the local authorities in each place, to provide them safe conduct to the land of Judea.

**5** This is a copy of the letter that Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:

**6** "Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people to their brothers the Spartans, greetings.

**7** Some time ago, a letter was sent to Onias the high priest from your king Arius, declaring that you are our brothers, as shown in the copy written below.

**8** Onias received the envoy with honor and accepted the letters, which contained a clear statement of friendship and alliance.

**9** Although we have no need of these things — having for our encouragement the holy scriptures that are in our hands —

**10** we venture to send this embassy to renew our bonds of brotherhood and friendship, lest we become strangers to you; for it has been a long time since you wrote to us.

**11** We therefore at every festival and on other appropriate occasions do not cease to remember you at the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.

**12** We rejoice in your honor and renown.

**13** As for us, many troubles and wars have surrounded us; the kings around us have fought against us.

**14** We were unwilling to trouble you or the other allies and friends we have with these wars,

**15** for we have the help that comes from Heaven to assist us, and we have been delivered from our enemies and our enemies have been brought low.

**16** So we chose Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, and we have sent them to the Romans to renew the earlier friendship and alliance with them.

**17** We gave them instructions to come to you as well, to greet you and to deliver to you this letter concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.

**18** Please send us your reply."

**19** This is the copy of the letter that had been sent to Onias:

**20** "Arius king of the Spartans to Onias the high priest, greetings.

**21** It has been discovered in a writing about the Spartans and the Jews that they are brothers and are of the family of Abraham.

**22** And now that we have come to know this, please write to us concerning your welfare.

**23** We do write to you ourselves: your cattle and your possessions are ours, and ours are yours. We therefore instruct that this be reported to you."

**24** Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had returned to fight against him with a larger force than before.

**25** He set out from Jerusalem and met them in the region of Hamath, giving them no chance to enter his territory.

**26** He sent spies into their camp; they came back and reported that the enemy was preparing a night attack.

**27** When the sun went down, Jonathan ordered his men to keep watch, weapons ready, prepared for battle throughout the night; and he posted sentinels all around the camp.

**28** When the enemy heard that Jonathan was prepared and ready for battle, they took fright, their hearts quailed, and they lit fires in their camp and slipped away.

**29** Jonathan and his men did not know this until morning, for they could see the fires still burning.

**30** Jonathan set out in pursuit but failed to overtake them, for they had already crossed the Jordan.

**31** Jonathan swung aside against the Nabateans known as Zabadeans, struck them, and took their plunder.

**32** He then broke camp and marched to Damascus, passing through the whole region.

**33** Simon went out and marched as far as Ashkelon and the neighboring fortresses; then he turned toward Joppa and seized it,

**34** for he had learned that they intended to hand the city over to Demetrius's men; and he stationed a garrison there to hold it.

**35** When Jonathan returned, he convened the council of elders of the people and consulted with them about building fortresses in Judea

**36** and raising the walls of Jerusalem higher, and about constructing a large barrier between the citadel and the city, to isolate the citadel from the city and cut off its supply lines.

**37** They gathered to work on the city; a section of the eastern wall had collapsed, and he rebuilt the section called Chaphenatha.

**38** Simon also built Adida in the Shephelah, fortified it, and erected gates with bars.

**39** Now Trypho was plotting to seize the kingship of Asia, put on the diadem, and strike against Antiochus the king.

**40** He was afraid that Jonathan would not allow it and would go to war against him, so he was looking for a way to seize and kill Jonathan. He set out and came to Beth-shan.

**41** Jonathan marched out to meet him with forty thousand picked warriors and came to Beth-shan.

**42** When Trypho saw that Jonathan had come with such a large army, he was afraid to raise a hand against him.

**43** He received Jonathan with honor, commended him to all his friends, gave him gifts, and ordered his troops to obey Jonathan as they would obey himself.

**44** Then he said to Jonathan: "Why have you put all this people to such trouble when there is no war between us?

**45** Dismiss them all to their homes. Choose a few men to accompany you and come with me to Ptolemais; I will hand it over to you, along with all the other remaining fortresses, the remaining troops, and all the officials. Then I will turn back and go home; that is why I came."

**46** Jonathan trusted him and did as he said. He dismissed his troops, and they returned to the land of Judea.

**47** He retained three thousand men, leaving two thousand in Galilee, while one thousand accompanied him.

**48** But when Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the men of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him; all who had come in with him they put to the sword.

**49** Trypho sent cavalry and infantry into Galilee and the Great Plain to annihilate Jonathan's troops.

**50** But when those troops were informed that Jonathan had been captured and killed, and all those with him, they encouraged one another and marched in close order, ready for battle.

**51** Seeing that they were prepared to fight to the death, those who were pursuing them turned back.

**52** They all reached the land of Judea safely; they mourned Jonathan and those with him and were in great fear, while all Israel lamented deeply.

**53** All the surrounding nations sought to wipe them out entirely, saying: "They have no leader, no helper; now let us attack them and wipe out their name from among men."
